header: Mr.Qurban Ali Malano for the applicant.
body: Mr.Muhammad Mahmood S. Khan Yousfi, Asstt: A.G.

The applicant/complainant has assailed the impugned bail order dated 07.12.2007 whereby the bail to the respondent No.1 was granted by the learned trial court and he has come for the cancellation of the same.

2. Brief facts of the case are that on telephonic message complainant and his PWs went to the house of respondent No.1 Abdul Haleem, there they found the respondent No.1 and other co-accused persons committing death of Mst.Sakina daughter of complainant by way of strangulating her throat. The respondent No.1 pointing his pistol towards complainant and his witnesses restrained them to come nearer for rescue of his daughter.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant/ complainant submits that the learned trial court has erred in granting the bail to the respondent No.1 on the ground that no active role has been assigned to the respondent No.1. On the contrary he has also mentioned in the bail order that the role attributed to the respondent No.1 was that he pointed the pistol and kept the complainant and his PWs under fear of death meaning thereby that the respondent No.1 has played active role facilitating the other co-accused persons to fire causing death of Mst.Sakina. PW Abdul Ghaffar and PW Muhammad Murad have fully implicated the respondent No.1 and also assigned the role of other co-accused persons in their statements recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C and 164 Cr.P.C who specifically stated that respondent No.1 Abdul Haleem was duly armed with pistol and by using the arm he put the complainant, deceased and PWs under fear and the other co-accused persons committed murder of Mst.Sakina. Had the respondent No.1 not restrained with arms complainant, deceased and the witnesses by targeting/pointing the pistol upon the complainant, deceased and PWs Abdul Ghaffar and Muhammad Murad, the remaining accused would not have successfully committed the murder of the deceased. The eye-witnesses have supported the contentions of the complainant incorporated in the F.I.R rather they have corroborated the complainant. There are reasonable grounds to believe that the respondent No.1 has committed the offence and the grant of bail to the applicant was not warranted.

4. The learned Asstt: A.G has not controverted the submissions made by the learned counsel for the applicant/complainant and submits that the respondent No.1 has been fully implicated by the eye-witnesses, nominated in the F.I.R and specific role has been assigned to him. The respondent No.1 has played an active role while restraining the complainant, deceased and PWs Abdul Ghaffar and Muhammad Murad. Due his active role the other co-accused persons have committed the murder of Mst.Sakina. He submits that the bail granted to the respondent No.1 Abdul Haleem be cancelled. He further submits that after recording statement of complainant and eye-witnesses and if his case for bail is made out, he can move the trial court for bail in the circumstances.

5. I have heard learned counsel for the applicant/complainant, learned Asstt: A.G and perused the material placed on the record and as discussed above, the active role is attributed to the respondent No.1 mentioned in the F.I.R and the same fact about the specific role assigned to the respondent No.1 has been described by the eye-witnesses who have fully implicated in their statements recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C and 164 Cr.P.C. there are reasonable grounds to believe that the respondent No.1 has committed the alleged offence. In my humble view the learned counsel for the applicant/complainant has succeeded to make out a case for the cancellation of bail of respondent No.1. The application is accordingly allowed. The bail granted to respondent No.1 Abdul Haleem is cancelled.
Cr.B.A. No.283 of 2007 of the co-accused will be heard and decided separately in accordance with law.
